title: Capacity fracture incident triage log
body:
Purpose: quick, sharable spreadsheet for tracking short-lived capacity failures ('capacity fractures') that cause cross-regional fallbacks, throttles, or elevated token burn. Use during initial triage to capture surface impact, quick mitigations, and one-off cost delta estimates. This is not the formal RCA record; link to RCA in the table and move to postmortem space when available.

How to use: add a row per unique incident (grouped by root trigger). Keep estimates conservative but explicit. If mitigation has reduced impact, update the row and add timestamped note.

Table (columns):
ID | Date | Impacted Route / Endpoint | Region(s) | Est. extra token burn / hr | Observed p95 latency (ms) | Failure mode | Trigger event | Primary owner | Secondary owner | Quick mitigation applied | Next action (24h) | RCA link | Notes
---|------|---------------------------|-----------|--------------------------:|----------------------------:|--------------|---------------|---------------|----------------|-----------------------|------------------|---------|------
CF-2029-061 | 2029-06-01 | /v1/generate (chat) | us-west1, us-east1 | 120k | 820 | queue pile-up -> autoscaler lag | sudden spike from SE pilot (unknown bot) | Marco Santos | Priya Reddy | bumped reserved capacity in us-west1 (temp) | implement rate-limit rule on pilot key; follow up with SE team | https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/CF-2029-061 | initial mitigation reduced error rate by 60% but latency still high in east due to regional routing mismatch
CF-2029-062 | 2029-06-02 | /v1/embeddings | eu-west1 | 65k | 450 | kernel OOM on quantized variant -> degraded to fp16 | untested model variant rolled by oncall canary | Jonah Kim | Aisha Patel | roll back to verified variant; pin model to last-known-good | add model-canary gating to rollout; add smoke test to CI | JIRA-INC-4821 | cost delta ~ $12/hr while rollback in progress; request dev-owner PR to add canary test
CF-2029-063 | 2029-06-03 | /v1/re-rank | ap-south1 | 8k | 210 | rate-limit cascading to downstream | new SE integration hitting batch endpoint incorrectly | Priya Reddy | Marco Santos | applied route-level reject for malformed requests | contact integrator; provide integration checklist |  | malformed requests stopped after reject; integrator released fix same day
CF-2029-064 | 2029-06-04 | /internal/cache-warm | us-central1 | 0 (latency cost only) | 310 | KV cache misses due to rotated instance IDs | infra deploy that replaced cache nodes without warmup | Aisha Patel | SRE rotational | pre-warm sequence and ramp traffic | create deployment prewarm script + orchestration gating | https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/CF-2029-064 | estimated invisible cost = customer retries; engineering still quantifying
CF-2029-065 | 2029-06-05 | /v1/generate (low-latency route) | global fallback | 200k | 1200 | region-level capacity exhausted -> global routing fallback | partner load reroute after their CDN outage | Marco Santos | Platform oncall | temporarily enabled burst pool and downgraded to quantized-compatible variant | negotiate partner alpha throttles; add partner-specific routing weight |  | partnered load resolved but cost exposure remains for 36h
CF-2029-066 | 2029-06-05 | embeddings-batch-worker | eu-central1 | 40k | 520 | misconfigured batch size causing memory oversubscribe | recent config change in dedicated pools | Jonah Kim | Infra team | reduced batch window and restarted workers | add config validation; create alert for batch-size anomalies | github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/2145 | next action: schedule infra postmortem; estimate extra spend $5-7/hr
CF-2029-067 | 2029-06-06 | /v1/tool-call | us-west2 | 3k | 180 | transient DNS flaps to model repository -> fallback to backup image | external registry hiccup | Priya Reddy | Aisha Patel | switched to local cached image | work with registry provider; add health-check for image fetch |  | no user-facing errors observed; internal throttle triggered

Summary metrics (live):
- Open incidents: 2 (CF-2029-061, CF-2029-065 still in active mitigation as of last scrub 2029-06-06)
- Incidents this week: 7
- Aggregate est. extra token burn (sum of active rows): ~456k tokens/hr (note: conservative, per-hour snapshot)
- Rough cost impact (ballpark): $40-70/hr depending on model mix and quantization (use product-cost quick calc sheet for precise)

Quick decisions made during triage:
- All SE pilot keys will be throttled by default for next 48h unless whitelisted (decision owner: Growth Eng)
- Model-canary gating: rollback if p95 exceeds 2x baseline in first 10m of canary (decision owner: Platform)

Open actions / owners (short):
- Create rate-limit rule for pilot keys (owner: Growth Eng) | due: 2029-06-07
- Add canary smoke test in model rollout CI (owner: Platform Eng) | due: 2029-06-10
- Run infra config postmortem for batch sizing (owner: Infra) | due: 2029-06-09
- Calculate precise cost delta for CF-2029-061 using billing export (owner: Finance ops) | due: 2029-06-08

Decision log (short notes):
- 2029-06-01 09:18 UTC: bumped reserved pool in us-west1 to avoid cascading failures; accepted incremental cost (~$300 for 6h) to keep customer SLAs intact. (owner: Marco)
- 2029-06-02 14:02 UTC: rolled back embedding variant to verified model; flagged PR for canary gating. (owner: Jonah)

Notes / heuristics for future scrubs:
- Use token-burn * 0.00012 USD as quick estimate for first-pass cost if model unknown (very rough).
- Prefer explicit per-route mitigation (reject/retry/backoff) over global reserved increases unless customer-affecting.
- Capture integrator/partner keys in incident row for follow-up (helps product/partnership owner)

Attachments referenced: billing quick-calc (sheet id: billing-quickcalc-2029), partner-integration-checklist (confluence id: partner-int-check).

Next scrub cadence: daily until incidents fall to zero, then weekly for 30 days postmortem completion. Last scrub: 2029-06-06 by Aisha Patel.
